messages:
Sophie (BorealHealth): hey team — since 03:12 UTC our Dedicated cluster is returning a bunch of 429s and spikes in tail latency. Customers see token-per-second limits hit even though we thought we had headroom. Noticed burst credits went to 0. Can you triage? :frowning:
Alex (support): sorry you're seeing that — can you paste a sample request id or trace id? we'll escalate to eng if it's infra.
Sophie (BorealHealth): request ids: req_8fa2c1, req_8fa2c8. Example payloads are normal chat completions, ~1k tokens expected, traffic burst from 6k TPS -> 22k TPS for ~45s.
Dinesh (SRE): grabbing audit logs. Initial quick check: admission controller rejected ~18% of inbound requests for that cluster during the window. BurstCredits reached 0 at 03:12:38 UTC.
Maya (oncall): pinging autoscaler metrics now. CPU/GPU utilisation didn't climb enough to trigger scale up — looks like admission headroom threshold = 20% on that pool, and current headroom went negative due to a sudden token-rate surge.
Luis (runtime): two immediate suspects: (1) noisy tenant — single client using long-context beams; (2) KV cache churn + large prefix causing slower per-token times. Also seeing model variant fallbacks for some routes which increased cost.
Alex (support): Sophie, did BorealHealth change any client side settings? concurrency or retry loops?
Sophie (BorealHealth): we rolled a batcher yesterday to parallelize sequences; we expected it to help latency but maybe increased effective TPS. We didn't update quota or inform Redwood.
Dinesh (SRE): repro plan: reproduce 20k TPS short burst against dedicated pool with same avg tokens. Need to test admission behaviour, credits, and autoscaler reaction time. Anyone with a quick sim script?
Luis (runtime): I can run a synthetic load test on a staging Dedicated pool. Quick patch: reduce max_concurrency for that route to 8 and enable conservative batching for that customer to drop effective TPS.
Maya (oncall): Logs: here's the admission controller snapshot (sanitized):
```
admission_window_s: 1
configured_headroom_pct: 20
burst_credits_total: 120000
burst_credits_used: 120000
current_tps: 22000
configured_tps_limit: 6000
rejections: 3800
```
Maya (oncall): autoscaler events show scale-up started at 03:13:22 but new nodes only became healthy at 03:14:10. That's >40s reaction time which allowed a prolonged SLO miss.
Dinesh (SRE): root causes so far: burst credits exhausted (policy misaligned with expected customer burst patterns), headroom threshold too tight for this pool's autoscaler latency, and noisy client increased KV-miss rates.
Alex (support): immediate mitigations we can push: (A) top-up burst credits for BorealHealth temporarily, (B) reduce route concurrency and enforce per-tenant rate limit, (C) enable automatic fallback to smaller model variant for that tenant. Which ones can we enact quickly?
Luis (runtime): I can flip (B) and (C) via feature flags for that tenant in console now. (A) requires billing/ops sign-off but we can do emergency top-up via infra script.
OpsBot: @ops-team emergency-burst-topup job queued for pool phoenix-dedicated-7. Requester: Alex. ETA ~2m.
Sophie (BorealHealth): please do (B) & (C) now. We can ask customers to retry with exponential backoff. Also we want a postmortem and a plan to avoid surprises.
Maya (oncall): doing a quick fix: applying temporary headroom bump to 35% for the pool and enabling faster scale aggressiveness for 10m window. Watching metrics.
Dinesh (SRE): running repro harness in staging to validate: script uses 100 concurrent clients sending 10 req/s each, 1k token sequences. I'll post results in 10m.
Luis (runtime): note for postmortem: consider changing default admission headroom to be adaptive by observed scale latency, and add burst-credit forecasting per-tenant based on 7/30d percentile.
Alex (support): Sophie — we'll follow up with a timeline for permanent controls and a credits reconciliation. Sorry for the outage; will keep you posted. :thumbsup:
Sophie (BorealHealth): thanks all. Appreciate the fast triage. Please include recommended guardrails so we don't hit this unpredictably again.
Dinesh (SRE): quick checklist for post-incident action items (for PMs & infra): [ ] adaptive headroom tuning, [ ] burst-credit alerts at 80% consumption, [ ] per-tenant burst profiles, [ ] autoscaler cold-start improvement, [ ] runtime KV-cache metrics per-tenant.
Luis (runtime): also adding a small runtime patch: detect long prefixes and circuit-break to smaller context after X ms to reduce KV churn. Will open PR after triage.
Maya (oncall): autoscaler and headroom changes holding steady. Rejections dropped to 0 within 45s after fixes. Monitoring for 30m.
Alex (support): updating ticket with mitigations and next steps. We'll schedule a postmortem with BorealHealth and share timeline for permanent changes.
OpsBot: burst-credit top-up completed on pool phoenix-dedicated-7 by job id jb_90431.
Sophie (BorealHealth): seeing errors clear up. Thank you everyone.
